To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the presence of multiple long-term conditions impacted on patients' illness representations in relation not only to the individual conditions themselves but also to the representation of the multiple conditions as a whole.

the presence of multimorbidities impacted on patient representations of individual conditions and on representations of multimorbidity, and that the latter included the dimensions of the burden of medications and the priorities among conditions and their management.
the presence of multimorbid conditions impacts on patient representations of individual conditions and of their multimorbidity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how patients with multiple conditions understand the nature of their conditions.
the impact of multiple long-term conditions on the patient experience of health and the implications of this for clinical practice.
how people with multiple long-term medical conditions make sense of and respond to their health problems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence of multiple chronic conditions impacts on illness perceptions and that the presence of multimorbidities itself is a representation of a chronic condition.
the presence of multiple chronic conditions has an impact on the way patients perceive their individual chronic diseases, as well as the way they perceive their overall health condition.

illness representations in patients with long-term conditions are impacted on by the presence of multimorbidities, which may be reflected in their representations of the individual conditions, and in the representation of multimorbid condition itself.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

multimorbidity impacts upon patient illness representations and that these representations need to be taken into account when designing interventions to improve the health of patients with multiple chronic conditions.

illness representation models can be applied to multimorbid long term conditions but that there are some modifications to the models that are required to reflect the impact of multimorbidities on patient illness representations.
illness representations are not simply the sum of representations of individual conditions but also include representations of multimorbidity and its impact.
The main takeaway from our work is that
illness representations are not just about individual long-term conditions.
illness representations are not just about a single condition but are influenced by the context of multiple conditions.
illness representation is not simply additive.
